newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm on pre-weekend dlr inflow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm on pre-weekend dlr inflow.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed early weakness to close firmer across the board on Thursday, after banks changed dollars to invest in the local money market over the weekend, traders said.

"There was some see-sawing during the session, but it was quiet in general," said a trader. "We closed with some dollars on offer as banks sold (dollar) positions to invest in peso debt instruments over the weekend."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.7 and 1.7 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.9050/7.9080 and 7.8870/7.8920 per dollar.
The same-day peso closed earlier 1.5 centavos firmer at 7.8940/7.8970.

Dealers noted that trade was light in the wake of Wednesday's Federal Open Market Committee decision not to change U.S. interest rates and due to a foreign exchange traders convention to be held this weekend.
Traders said they expected the peso to be under pressure over the coming weeks due to corporations closing month-end positions and a seasonal spike in inflation.
